<span class="section-code">01 / RESEARCH QUESTION</span>

## Where is the computer systems design workforce heading?

Our analysis connects employer demand with the skills and career opportunities shaping computer systems design and related services. Rather than examining job counts alone, we evaluate what companies need, where opportunities are concentrated, and how candidates can prepare.

:::

<span class="section-code">03 / FINDINGS</span>

## What the evidence shows

All three findings are complete. Each links to the page carrying the full analysis.

:::

::: {.finding-row}

<span class="finding-id">F.01</span>

<div>
<strong>Market structure</strong>

Data science and data engineering roles lead the 1,790 postings. California has the most postings with a known state, the median advertised salary is $151,475, and 41% of postings are remote or hybrid.
</div>

<span class="finding-status">COMPLETE</span>

:::

::: {.finding-row}

<span class="finding-id">F.02</span>

<div>
<strong>Skill signals</strong>

Python and SQL each appear in more than 60% of postings and sit among the team's largest gaps, alongside data pipelines. Business and communication skills already meet what employers ask for.
</div>

<span class="finding-status">COMPLETE</span>

:::

::: {.finding-row}

<span class="finding-id">F.03</span>

<div>
<strong>Career opportunity</strong>

Job title alone separates higher-paying postings only 59% of the time. Adding skills, location, and education raises that to 78%. The skills most associated with higher pay are not the ones employers request most often.
</div>

<span class="finding-status">COMPLETE</span>

:::
